rows.source_location: PubMed abstract (Materials and methods, Results); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04419350 registry record (Design, Registered outcomes, Eligibility); no registry results posted
rows.diagnosis: ADJACENT: localized acquired hypomelanosis (registry: secondary to any insult, post-inflammatory or iatrogenic, larger than 3 cm); not IGH; whether any IGH was included is not in abstract
rows.design: randomized controlled trial; abstract says lesions randomized; registry says each treated area was split into two halves randomized by sealed envelope (within-lesion split, so the control half is not independent); registry masking DOUBLE (investigator, outcomes assessor)
rows.body_site: not in abstract (registry eligibility allows any site except genitalia)
rows.intervention: single session of microneedling, dermaroller 1.5-mm needles
rows.comparator: no treatment (untreated half of the same area, per registry)
rows.endpoint_definition: peripheral tanning (skin mapping of lesion surface area through transparent stencil paper, per registry)
rows.arm_result: median peripheral tanning observed in 80% of lesions
rows.patient_noticeability: not in abstract (patient satisfaction was measured; result not in abstract)
rows.texture_or_scar: not in abstract (scarring was a registered safety outcome; result not in abstract)
rows.uncertainty: Abstract wording 'median peripheral tanning was observed in 80% of lesions' is ambiguous: it may be a median tanned fraction or the share of lesions with any tanning. Not an IGH study: target is localized acquired hypomelanosis larger than 3 cm (registry), IGH spots are small. No between-arm statistics or p-values in abstract. Control is the untreated half of the same area (registry), so spillover or a systemic effect cannot be separated; the untreated arm improved about as much as the treated arm. Medians given without IQR or denominators. Single session, so 3 months after start equals 3 months after the final treatment.
rows.citation: Elhoshy K, Ibrahim J, Hafez V. Microneedling in Localized Acquired Hypomelanosis: A Randomized Controlled Trial. Dermatol Surg 2025;51(3):257-262

verifier.notes: Rows are numbered from 0, as in the quotes list. row 2, analysis_unit: abstract gives no unit for the physician GAI median and the record itself says 'unit of the median not stated'; 'lesion' is an inferred value and needs [square brackets]; registry says each area was 'split into two halves then randomized', so the arm unit may be a half-area. row 3, analysis_unit: same as row 2. row 4, analysis_unit: same as row 2 (VESTA median, unit not stated). row 5, analysis_unit: same as row 4. row 8, analysis_unit: same as row 2 (surface tanning median, unit not stated). row 9, analysis_unit: same as row 8. row 2, uncertainty: registry says 'One unblinded and 2 blinded investigators assessed the global improvement', which conflicts with 'Masking: DOUBLE (INVESTIGATOR, OUTCOMES_ASSESSOR)'; an unblinded assessor in the physician GAI is not recorded as a weakness. row 3, uncertainty: same as row 2. rows 0 to 9, uncertainty: abstract conclusion says 'localized acquired hypomelanosis in normal-texture and scarred skin', so the sample mixed scarred and normal-texture skin at baseline; this heterogeneity is absent from uncertainty in every row (10 cells). Checked and supported: every quote is in the source; arm_result values match the right arm in all 10 rows; time_from_last_treatment 3 months is supported by 'a single session ... Three months later' and '3 months post treatment'; patients_enrolled 20; outcome_tier partial_repigmentation is the weakest reading; missing-data wording is correct.
